name: Tomyang
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.note: Glottolog: retired ISO code, merged into Yamphu; 'the only Tomyang data collected was a Swadish 100 words list'

sources.citation: Hilty, Holly J. & Jessica R. Mitchell. 2014. Yamphu: A Sociolinguistic Survey. SIL Electronic Survey Report 2014-007.
sources.note: No mention of Tomyang at all (grep); per earlier reading no stress/accent statement anywhere.

sources.citation: ISO 639-3 Registration Authority. 2006 [adopted 2007-07-18]. Change Request 2006-109: retire [tmx] Tomyang, merge into [ybi] Yamphu. SIL International.
sources.note: Nothing; identity only: 82% lexical similarity with Yamphu, the only Tomyang data ever collected is one Swadesh-100 list (21% Nepali loans), source = Pokharel 2001.

sources.citation: Ebert, Karen H. 2003. Kiranti languages: an overview. In Thurgood & LaPolla (eds.), The Sino-Tibetan Languages, 505-517. London: Routledge.
sources.note: Sec. 2.1 Phonology mentions Yamphu only for vowel length in closed syllables (ce?ma 'plough' vs cee?ma 'spit'); nothing on Yamphu stress.

sources.citation: Pokharel, Madhav P. 2001. A phonological sketch from the Tomyang wordlist. Nepalese Linguistics 18: 1-4. Kathmandu: Linguistic Society of Nepal.
sources.note: Nothing. Sec. 3 'Phonology' (pp. 2-4) covers a six-vowel system, breathy /ɦ/, gemination, absence of vowel length, diphthongs, vowel sequences, glottal stop with syllable-final /t/, consonant inventory, nasalization, [ḍ] and retroflex flap; no mention of stress, accent or tone. Printed p. 4 is a misprint duplicating p. 3, so the article's closing lines/references are lost in the volume itself.

sources.citation: Gerber, Pascal. 2023. Vergleich und Rekonstruktion der Oberarun-Sprachen (Kiranti): Mit einer Skizze des Westmewahang. PhD dissertation, Universität Bern, xxvii+905 pp.
